**Executive Summary**

CorpStage is an **Intelligent Enterprise Operating Center** --- not an
ESG platform, not a compliance tool, not a reporting portal.

It exists for one purpose: to improve the quality of executive judgment.
Every signal it ingests --- operational, financial, regulatory,
competitive, environmental, social --- is translated into business
language and surfaced as a ranked, evidenced, financially-translated
decision input.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **The Platform Identity --- Non-Negotiable**                          |
|                                                                       |
| CorpStage is an Intelligent Enterprise Operating Center.              |
|                                                                       |
| Sustainability signals are one of many inputs. Business decisions are |
| the only output.                                                      |
|                                                                       |
| Compliance emerges invisibly from enterprise understanding. It is     |
| never the primary frame.                                              |
|                                                                       |
| The executive should never encounter the words ESG, Scope, or         |
| Framework on any primary screen.                                      |
|                                                                       |
| Every metric speaks money, risk, or strategic consequence --- never   |
| framework language.                                                   |

every layer, every screen, every data point in the entire CorpStage
architecture must trace back to this document. If it does not serve the
Enterprise Mental Model or answer a Canonical Executive Question, it
does not exist in CorpStage.*

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Critical Distinction --- Mental Model vs Intelligence Library**     |
|                                                                       |
| Enterprise Mental Model = How CorpStage thinks about an enterprise.   |
| The conceptual framework. The worldview.                              |
|                                                                       |
| Canonical Intelligence Library = The atomic intelligence points. The  |
| data. The specific facts to be known.                                 |

| The lens must exist before the data has meaning.                      |

**Part A --- The Enterprise Mental Model**

The Enterprise Mental Model is CorpStage\'s complete answer to one
foundational question: \"What must an intelligent platform truly
understand about a business --- before it can be genuinely useful to the
people running it?\" Not how to acquire that understanding. Not how to
display it. Simply --- what must be known.

This model has six dimensions. Every intelligence point in the Canonical
Intelligence Library maps to one of them. Every screen in the Master
Screen Architecture illuminates one or more of them. Every question
CorpStage asks deepens its understanding of one of them.

The six dimensions are not data categories. They are living,
interconnected aspects of a real enterprise --- each one influencing the
others, each one changing continuously, each one carrying financial
consequence.

**Dimension 1 --- IDENTITY**

*What this enterprise fundamentally is*

Before understanding how an enterprise performs, CorpStage must
understand what it is. Identity is the skeleton on which all other
understanding is built. Risk exposure attaches to legal entities, not to
organisational structures. Regulatory obligations attach to
jurisdictions of operation, not to business units. Governance
accountability attaches to board membership, not to job titles.

**1.1 Legal & Ownership Structure**

The complete legal architecture of the enterprise. Every incorporated
entity. Every jurisdiction of incorporation. Every ownership
relationship --- subsidiaries, associates, joint ventures, special
purpose vehicles. Shareholding percentages. Ultimate beneficial
ownership. Board composition at each entity level.

**1.2 Organisational Architecture**

How the enterprise is structured for operating purposes. Business units,
divisions, segments, and their relationships. Profit and loss ownership.
Cost centre structure. Management accountability at each level. How
strategy flows from group to entity to facility.

**1.3 Operational Footprint**

Every facility, site, plant, office, warehouse, data centre, and
operational location the enterprise controls or depends on. Geographic
coordinates. Operational type and function. Production capacity.
Workforce size. Asset value. Operational criticality.

**1.4 Sector & Industry Context**

The primary and secondary industries in which the enterprise operates.
Value chain position. Business model fundamentals. Revenue model. Sector
context determines what matters --- every intelligence benchmark,
regulatory mapping, and peer comparison is sector-specific.

**Dimension 2 --- OPERATIONS**

*How the enterprise actually runs*

Understanding what an enterprise does operationally --- not just what it
reports --- is the difference between intelligence and data. CorpStage
must understand the mechanics of value creation, not just its financial
outputs.

**2.1 Value Creation Process**

What the enterprise does to create value --- what it makes, how it makes
it, what inputs it requires, what processes it runs, what outputs it
produces. Every operational risk manifests at the point of value
creation.

**2.2 Input Dependencies**

Everything the enterprise depends on to operate. Raw materials and
sources. Energy type, quantity, source. Water volume and criticality.
Technology and digital infrastructure. Critical equipment and its
provenance. Input dependency is where operational and financial risk
intersect.

**2.3 Supply Chain Architecture**

The complete supply network: Tier 1 direct suppliers, Tier 2 and Tier 3
critical indirect suppliers, customer base with Business Resilience
requirements embedded in commercial agreements, logistics and
distribution network. A Tier 2 supplier in a high-risk geography can
disrupt production faster than any internal operational failure.

**2.4 Human Capital Architecture**

Total workforce size and composition. Direct employees vs contractors.
Critical skill concentrations. Unionisation and industrial relations.
Safety performance by facility. Workforce cost as a proportion of
revenue. People are both the greatest operational asset and the greatest
operational vulnerability.

**2.5 Technology & Digital Infrastructure**

Core technology systems and their criticality. Digital operational
dependencies. Data assets and their business value. Cybersecurity
exposure profile. Technology transition obligations. Digital capability
gaps relative to competitive requirements.

**Dimension 3 --- COMMITMENTS**

*What the enterprise has promised, to whom, and by when*

This is the dimension that no platform has systematically built. Every
enterprise has made hundreds of commitments --- to different audiences,
in different documents, at different times, with different levels of
precision and legal enforceability. Nobody tracks them all. Nobody maps
them against operational reality. CorpStage does.

**3.1 Financial Commitments**

Debt obligations and covenants. Bond prospectus representations ---
particularly Financial Obligations with Performance Conditions where financial terms
are tied to performance targets. Credit facility conditions. Dividend
commitments. Capital expenditure guidance. Earnings guidance.

**3.2 Regulatory Commitments**

Obligations made to regulators --- operating licences and their
conditions, environmental permits and their limits, consent agreements,
remediation plans, decommissioning obligations. Regulatory commitments
have legal force. Non-compliance triggers enforcement, fines, or licence
revocation.

**3.3 Investor & Public Commitments**

Targets and timelines disclosed in annual reports. Commitments made on
earnings calls. Strategic Commitments. Diversity and
inclusion targets. Any quantified target the CEO, CFO, or Chair has
communicated publicly. Investor commitments are increasingly legally
material.

**3.4 Customer & Supplier Commitments**

Business Resilience performance requirements embedded in customer contracts.
Supplier code of conduct obligations. Transition Commitment claims on
products or services that carry legal weight under consumer protection
law. Delivery, quality, and service commitments with financial penalty
clauses.

**3.5 Employee & Community Commitments**

Commitments made to employees in collective agreements, employment
contracts, or public announcements. Commitments made to communities ---
local employment, community investment, environmental standards.
Commitments from M&A processes that were conditions of regulatory
approval or community acceptance.

**Dimension 4 --- EXPOSURES**

*What can hurt the enterprise, and how badly*

Exposure is not risk in the traditional sense. It is the universe of
forces that can reduce the enterprise\'s ability to create value, meet
its obligations, or maintain its strategic direction. CorpStage maps all
exposures, not just the ones that appear in risk registers.

**4.1 Physical & Climate Exposures**

Acute physical risks: extreme weather events --- flooding, heat stress,
drought, storms, wildfires. Chronic physical risks: water availability
decline, average temperature increase, sea level rise. Mapped at
facility level. Assessed across time horizons --- current, 5-year,
15-year, 30-year.

**4.2 Transition & Regulatory Exposures**

Energy Cost & Transition Exposure: the financial consequence of current and
projected transition costs. Energy transition exposure: stranded asset risk
in transition-exposed assets. Regulatory transition: new laws requiring
capital investment, operational change, or creating financial penalties
if not met.

**4.3 Market & Competitive Exposures**

Customer concentration risk. Commodity price exposure. Competitive
disruption risk --- are competitors investing in capabilities that could
erode market position? Pricing power erosion from Business Resilience
requirements creating cost without ability to recover through pricing.

**4.4 Financial Exposures**

Liquidity risk. Refinancing risk. Interest rate sensitivity. Foreign
exchange exposure. Green finance eligibility --- is the enterprise
positioned to access preferential green financing, or is deteriorating
performance closing that window?

**4.5 Reputational & Relationship Exposures**

Investor sentiment trends. Activist investor risk. Media and civil
society monitoring. Customer perception risk. Regulatory relationship
risk --- does the enterprise have a constructive or adversarial
relationship with its key regulators?

**4.6 Operational Continuity Exposures**

Single points of failure in operations --- facilities, systems, or
suppliers whose loss would halt critical production. Workforce
concentration risk. Technology dependency risk --- systems with no
redundancy. Supply chain concentration risk.

**Dimension 5 --- RELATIONSHIPS**

*Who the enterprise depends on, and who depends on it*

No enterprise operates in isolation. Every enterprise is embedded in a
web of relationships --- each one carrying dependencies, obligations,
influence, and risk. CorpStage maps this web and understands the
financial materiality of each relationship.

**5.1 Capital Relationships**

Shareholders --- their identity, investment thesis, expectations, and
activism risk. Lenders --- their terms, covenants, and refinancing
timelines. Rating agencies --- current ratings and rating trajectories.
Performance-Linked Financial Obligation providers --- performance
measurement and consequences for missed targets.

**5.2 Commercial Relationships**

Major customers --- revenue concentration, contract terms,
Business Resilience requirements, renewal timelines. Key suppliers --- spend
concentration, single-source risk, geographic risk, financial stability.
Distribution and logistics partners --- reliability, concentration, and
transition risk.

**5.3 Regulatory Relationships**

Primary regulators --- the nature of the relationship, current
regulatory posture, pending reviews, enforcement history.
Standard-setting bodies. Government relationships at national and local
level affecting permitting, operating conditions, and policy exposure.

**5.4 Workforce Relationships**

Trade unions and their relationships with management. Employee
representative bodies. Key talent communities. Executive and senior
leadership relationships --- the people without whom the enterprise\'s
strategy cannot be executed.

**5.5 Community & Civil Society Relationships**

Local communities surrounding major facilities --- their concerns,
organised influence, and ability to affect operating licences and
capital projects. NGOs and civil society organisations. Media
organisations covering the sector. Academic institutions researching
areas material to the enterprise\'s risk profile.

**Dimension 6 --- TRAJECTORY**

*Where the enterprise is actually heading, and whether its stated
direction matches its real momentum*

Trajectory is the dimension that separates a backward-looking
intelligence platform from a forward-looking decision system. CorpStage
does not just understand where the enterprise is. It understands where
it is going --- and whether those are the same thing.

**6.1 Strategic Commitments & Capital Plans**

The stated strategic direction --- where the enterprise intends to be in
three, five, and ten years. The capital investment programme committed
to deliver that direction. Critically: whether the capital committed is
sufficient to deliver the strategy stated. This is the most common and
most dangerous strategic blind spot in corporate governance.

**6.2 Performance Trajectory**

The trend lines --- not the snapshots --- of every material performance
dimension. Trajectory is always more important than position. An
enterprise at 40% of target but accelerating is in a fundamentally
different position than one at 60% of target but decelerating.

**6.3 Commitment Delivery Trajectory**

For every commitment made in Dimension 3 --- what is the current rate of
progress, and does that rate deliver the commitment by the deadline?
This is the Commitment Integrity signal. Calculated continuously. Alerts
automatically when the gap requires executive intervention.

**6.4 Competitive Position Trajectory**

How the enterprise\'s position relative to peers is moving across all
dimensions of business resilience. Are competitors investing more
aggressively? Are they accessing cheaper capital? Are they attracting
talent more effectively?

**6.5 Regulatory Trajectory**

Where the regulatory environment is heading --- not just what the
current rules are, but what the direction of regulatory travel means for
the enterprise. Which regulations under consultation will become law?
Which current exemptions are at risk of being removed?

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **The Six Dimensions --- Interconnection**                            |
|                                                                       |
| Identity shapes which Exposures apply --- a legal entity in Germany   |
| faces Regulatory Cost Exposure obligations an entity in Singapore does not.               |
|                                                                       |
| Operations determine which Commitments are achievable --- a transition-cost    |
| commitment requiring a process change must be assessed against        |
| operational cost.                                                     |
|                                                                       |
| Commitments create Exposures --- a Performance-Linked Financial Obligation covenant creates a      |
| financial exposure that did not exist before the bond was issued.     |
|                                                                       |
| Relationships affect Trajectory --- a major investor\'s changing      |
| requirements can alter strategic options faster than any internal     |
| review.                                                               |
|                                                                       |
| Trajectory reveals Commitment integrity gaps --- the most material    |
| intelligence CorpStage produces is the gap between what was promised  |
| and where trajectory is actually taking the enterprise.               |
|                                                                       |
| This interconnection is why CorpStage cannot be built as a collection |
| of separate modules.                                                  |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

**Part B --- The Canonical Executive Questions**

Twelve questions. One per Intelligence Center screen. Written in exact
executive language --- the words a CEO or CFO would use at 7am, not the
words a product manager would use in a requirements document.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Four Components of Each Question**                                  |
|                                                                       |
| The Question --- one sentence, in business language, unambiguous.     |
|                                                                       |
| The Decision It Enables --- what action becomes possible when this    |
| question is answered?                                                 |
|                                                                       |
| The Consequence of Not Knowing --- what goes wrong if this goes       |
| unanswered?                                                           |
|                                                                       |
| The Financial Translation --- what does the answer ultimately mean in |
| money, risk, or capital?                                              |
|                                                                       |
| These twelve questions are the filter for all subsequent architecture |
| decisions.                                                            |
|                                                                       |
| If a feature, data point, intelligence rule, or screen element does   |
| not serve at least one of them --- it does not exist in CorpStage.    |

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **SECTION I --- Executive Language Standard (Binding)**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

Every label, prompt, heading, metric name, notification, and narrative
in CorpStage must pass the business language test. If a sustainability
professional must translate it for the CFO, it has failed.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Never Say**        **Always Say**       **Why It Matters**
  -------------------- -------------------- -----------------------------
  **ESG Score**        **Business           CFOs do not have an ESG
                       Resilience Index**   budget line. They have a
                                            resilience budget.

  **Carbon Emissions** **Energy Cost &      Carbon is only interesting
                       Transition           when it costs money.
                       Exposure**           

  **Scope 1 / 2 / 3**  **Direct /           Scope language means nothing
                       Procurement / Value  to a CFO or CEO.
                       Chain Cost**         

  **Water Stress**     **Operational        Operations language, not
                       Continuity Risk**    environmental language.

  **Diversity          **Talent             Talent is a financial
  Metrics**            Competitiveness**    variable. Diversity is a
                                            political one.

  **CSRD Compliance**  **Regulatory Cost    The executive cares about
                       Exposure**           cost and risk, not acronyms.

  **Sustainability     **Strategic          Commitments are owned by the
  Target**             Commitment**         CEO. Targets are owned by the
                                            CSO.

  **ESG Framework**    **Reporting          Obligations have legal and
                       Obligation**         financial consequences.
                                            Frameworks do not.

  **Greenwashing       **Commitment         Integrity risk is a
  Risk**               Integrity Risk**     board-level concern.
                                            Greenwashing is a media term.

  **Social             **Workforce &        Risk language activates CFO
  Performance**        Community Risk**     attention. Social language
                                            does not.

  **Net Zero Target**  **Decarbonisation    Plans have budgets. Targets
                       Cost Plan**          do not.

  **Materiality        **Business Impact    Every executive understands
  Assessment**         Prioritisation**     impact prioritisation.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **SECTION J --- Architecture Summary & The 39 Laws Quick Reference**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**What CorpStage Is --- In One Paragraph**

CorpStage is an Intelligent Enterprise Operating Center that
progressively understands a business --- from uploaded documents and
public filings on day one, to connected operational systems over time
--- and translates everything it learns into financial consequences,
forward-looking risks, and ranked actions. It knows what the
organisation has promised the world, what it is actually doing, and
where the gap is widening. It questions the assumptions executives are
not questioning. It remembers every decision and its outcome. And it
surfaces all of this through a calm, always-current Action Center ---
evidenced, auditable, and always translated into the language of money,
risk, and strategic consequence.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Who Buys CorpStage --- and Why**                                    |
|                                                                       |
| CFO buys it: because the Resilience P&L finally shows what business   |
| risk costs in financial terms.                                        |
|                                                                       |
| CEO buys it: because the Question Engine asks what the organisation   |
| cannot ask itself.                                                    |
|                                                                       |
| Board buys it: because the Living Memory protects oversight and       |
| personal accountability.                                              |
|                                                                       |
| General Counsel buys it: because Contradiction Detection and the      |
| audit trail are legal protection.                                     |
|                                                                       |
| COO buys it: because the Action Center surfaces operational risks     |
| before they become crises.                                            |
|                                                                       |
| CRO buys it: because the Risk Lens gives a risk register view of the  |
| same intelligence the CFO and CSO use.                                |
|                                                                       |
| The CSO uses it --- in the Regulatory & Framework Detail Lens. But the CSO does not  |
| initiate the purchase. That is the strategic positioning shift.       |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Commitment Integrity --- The Scenario That Closes Deals**           |
|                                                                       |
| CEO commits to net-zero by 2040 on a Q2 earnings call. CorpStage      |
| tracks every capital allocation decision since. By FY24: zero capex   |
| earmarked for decarbonisation. Energy intensity up 8%. Renewable      |
| share down from 22% to 18%.                                           |
|                                                                       |

**2.2 --- Enterprise Relationship Model**

CorpStage is synthesis intelligence, not data warehousing. The
intelligence it generates is not found in any single domain --- it
emerges from the relationships between domains. Understanding these
relationships is as important as understanding the domains themselves.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Relationship Type**           **Definition and example**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Causal**                      A state in one domain directly causes a
                                  state in another. Supplier
                                  concentration (D06) causes cost
                                  volatility (D03). Physical climate
                                  exposure (D10) causes operational
                                  continuity risk (D04).

  **Amplifying**                  A state in one domain makes a state in
                                  another worse or better. Poor workforce
                                  resilience (D08) amplifies the impact
                                  of operational disruptions (D04).
                                  Strong financial resilience (D15)
                                  dampens the impact of market shocks
                                  (D03).

  **Revealing**                   Intelligence in one domain reveals a
                                  hidden truth in another. Observed
                                  operational data (D04) reveals the gap
                                  between stated and real performance,
                                  surfacing behavioural dynamics (D14).

  **Constraining**                The state of one domain limits the
                                  options available in another. Financial
                                  leverage (D03) constrains strategic
                                  investment options (D13). Workforce
                                  capability gaps (D08) constrain
                                  operational transformation speed (D04).
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**2.3 --- Enterprise State Model**

CorpStage must understand and track six states simultaneously ---
because the most important executive questions are not about what is
happening now, but about what happened before, what direction things are
moving, and what is going to happen next.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **State**                       **What it captures and what it powers**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Current**                     What is objectively true about the
                                  enterprise at this moment from
                                  confirmed, high-confidence
                                  intelligence. Powers: Enterprise Health
                                  Command Center, Action Center priority
                                  ranking, all financial materiality
                                  calculations.

  **Emerging**                    What is beginning to form --- signals
                                  not yet confirmed but consistent and
                                  directional enough to warrant
                                  attention. Powers: Early warning
                                  intelligence, the Question Engine, the
                                  Regulatory Intelligence screen.

  **Stressed**                    Where a domain, entity, facility, or
                                  relationship is under pressure
                                  exceeding normal operating parameters.
                                  Powers: Risk Heatmap, Operational
                                  Continuity Intelligence, escalation
                                  logic of the Action Center.

  **Committed**                   The state the enterprise has promised
                                  to reach --- through targets,
                                  covenants, public commitments, and
                                  regulatory obligations. Powers:
                                  Commitment Integrity Monitor, Target
                                  trajectory assessment, Performance-Linked Financial Obligation
                                  covenant tracking.

  **Future --- Projected**        Where the enterprise\'s current
                                  trajectory will take it --- a
                                  probabilistic range, not a point
                                  estimate. The gap between Projected
                                  Future State and Committed State is the
                                  Commitment Integrity Signal --- the
                                  most important signal CorpStage
                                  generates.

  **Observed**                    What external signals, independent of
                                  management reporting, suggest about the
                                  enterprise\'s actual condition. Powers:
                                  Behavioural Dynamics detection,
                                  Contradiction identification between
                                  declared and observed.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**2.4 --- Enterprise Pressure Model**

Risk is a threat with a probability and an impact. A pressure is
different --- a sustained force that shapes decisions, constrains
options, and influences behaviour continuously. CorpStage thinks in
pressures because pressures explain why enterprises make the decisions
they make.

**Internal Pressures**

**Cost Pressure**

Sustained force to reduce costs from margin compression, competitive
pricing, covenant requirements, or investor expectations. When extreme,
it overrides stated strategic priorities.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **CorpStage signal:**                                                 |
|                                                                       |
| When cost pressure indicators rise, CorpStage monitors which          |
| commitments and investments are being cut first, and whether those    |
| cuts create future risks.                                             |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

**Capability Pressure**

Gap between the capabilities the enterprise needs to execute its
strategy and the capabilities it currently has. One of the most common
causes of strategic under-delivery.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **CorpStage signal:**                                                 |
|                                                                       |
| When strategic ambition consistently outpaces execution, and when the |
| capability investment required to close the gap is below what the     |
| strategy requires.                                                    |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

**Execution Pressure**

Pressure to deliver near-term commitments that crowds out longer-term
strategic investments. The most common cause of commitment integrity
failures.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **CorpStage signal:**                                                 |
|                                                                       |
| When near-term pressure is consuming the capital or management        |
| attention required to deliver long-term commitments. Flags            |
| commitments structurally at risk.                                     |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

**Liquidity Pressure**

Pressure arising from cash availability relative to obligations. Affects
every other decision --- strategic, operational, and workforce.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **CorpStage signal:**                                                 |
|                                                                       |
| Liquidity headroom trends. Covenant proximity. The interaction        |
| between liquidity pressure and commitment deliverability.             |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

**External Pressures**

**Regulatory Pressure**

Volume, speed, and stringency of regulatory change across the
enterprise\'s jurisdictions. Increasing globally and a primary driver of
capital reallocation and strategic repositioning in every sector.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **CorpStage signal:**                                                 |
|                                                                       |
| Regulatory pipeline density --- how many material changes in          |
| development? Financial consequence modelling --- what does full       |
| compliance cost, by jurisdiction and timeline?                        |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

**Climate & Physical Pressure**

Increasing physical stress on assets and operations. Long-duration
pressures on facilities built for a climate that no longer exists or
will not exist within their operational lifetime.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **CorpStage signal:**                                                 |
|                                                                       |
| Physical risk scores by facility, updated as climate science          |
| advances. Insurance market signals --- where are premiums rising or   |
| coverage being withdrawn?                                             |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

**Competitive Pressure**

Sustained force from competitors for customers, talent, capital,
regulatory favour, and strategic positioning. The continuous movement of
relative position.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **CorpStage signal:**                                                 |
|                                                                       |
| Competitor investment signals --- where are competitors deploying     |
| capital that the enterprise is not? Talent flow signals --- where are |
| people leaving for competitors?                                       |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

**Geopolitical Pressure**

Pressure from political instability, policy uncertainty, sanctions,
tariff changes, and conflict in geographies where the enterprise
operates, sources, or sells.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **CorpStage signal:**                                                 |
|                                                                       |
| Geopolitical risk scores for all material operating and sourcing      |
| geographies. Supply chain concentration in high-geopolitical-risk     |
| regions.                                                              |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

**Customer Expectation Pressure**

Increasing requirements from major customers --- Business Resilience
standards, supply chain transparency, transition-cost intensity limits --- now
with revenue consequences for non-compliance.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **CorpStage signal:**                                                 |
|                                                                       |
| Customer Business Resilience requirement inventory. Revenue at risk from   |
| contract conditions the enterprise cannot currently satisfy.          |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

**2.5 --- Enterprise Materiality Model**

An intelligence signal is material when it matters enough to change an
executive decision, alter a capital allocation, or require a governance
response. Everything else is noise. CorpStage uses seven dimensions.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Dimension**                   **Definition and threshold**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Financial**                   Quantifiable impact on revenue, margin,
                                  cash, cost of capital, or enterprise
                                  value. The primary filter. Threshold:
                                  impact exceeds defined % of EBITDA or
                                  revenue.

  **Strategic**                   Affects ability to execute stated
                                  strategy or requires revision of that
                                  strategy. Threshold: changes
                                  probability of strategy delivery by a
                                  defined threshold, or makes a funded
                                  commitment undeliverable.

  **Operational**                 Affects ability to produce, deliver, or
                                  serve customers above a defined
                                  minimum. Threshold: threatens
                                  production continuity at a facility
                                  above a defined revenue or capacity
                                  contribution.

  **Ecosystem**                   Affects relationships with suppliers,
                                  customers, capital providers,
                                  regulators, communities. Threshold:
                                  threatens a relationship whose
                                  disruption consumes material management
                                  attention or capital.

  **Reputational**                Affects reputation with audiences that
                                  influence ability to operate, attract
                                  capital, or attract talent. Threshold:
                                  reaches an audience with ability to
                                  take action with financial or
                                  operational consequences.

  **Regulatory**                  Affects compliance status with
                                  obligations carrying legal, financial,
                                  or operating licence consequences.
                                  Threshold: non-compliance results in
                                  fine, enforcement action, or mandatory
                                  change above a defined threshold.

  **Leadership**                  Requires a response only an executive
                                  or board member can authorise.
                                  Threshold: decision sits above
                                  delegated authority of operational
                                  management, or governance implications
                                  require board awareness.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**2.6 --- Enterprise Truth Model**

Not all intelligence is equal. CorpStage must distinguish between seven
types of truth --- because mixing truth types without labelling them is
how AI systems erode executive trust.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Truth Type**                  **Definition and how CorpStage handles
                                  it**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Deterministic**               Known with certainty from reliable
                                  primary sources --- a legal entity
                                  registration, a signed contract term, a
                                  regulatory filing. Accepted at face
                                  value. Never presented with a
                                  confidence range.

  **Probabilistic**               Known with quantifiable uncertainty ---
                                  a forecast, a risk probability
                                  estimate, a scenario outcome. Always
                                  expressed as a range with central
                                  estimate and confidence interval. Never
                                  presented as fact.

  **Behavioural**                 Observed patterns of decision-making
                                  that reveal the real operating logic of
                                  the enterprise --- distinct from its
                                  stated logic. Built from pattern
                                  analysis over time. Surfaced as a
                                  question or observation, never an
                                  assertion.

  **Declared**                    What the enterprise has stated --- in
                                  annual reports, investor presentations,
                                  regulatory filings. Stored verbatim
                                  with source, date, and context. Always
                                  compared with observed truth to
                                  identify divergence.

  **Observed**                    What external, independent signals
                                  suggest about the enterprise\'s actual
                                  condition. Weighted by source
                                  reliability. Divergence between
                                  observed and declared is a primary
                                  contradiction detection signal.

  **Derived**                     Conclusions CorpStage reaches through
                                  synthesis and reasoning across multiple
                                  inputs. Most valuable --- and most
                                  important to handle carefully. Full
                                  evidence chain always disclosed. Never
                                  presented as fact.

  **Contested**                   Two or more credible sources give
                                  conflicting information. Not a data
                                  quality failure --- a signal in itself.
                                  Both positions held and displayed.
                                  Never resolved by the system alone.
                                  Always escalated.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**2.7 --- Enterprise Intelligence States**

For every intelligence element, CorpStage holds an understanding at one
of eight maturity levels --- about the quality of understanding and the
confidence with which CorpStage can act on what it knows.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Intelligence State**          **Definition and CorpStage action**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Unknown**                     No information. An active state that
                                  triggers acquisition activity. Flags as
                                  intelligence gap. Assesses financial
                                  materiality of the gap.

  **Suspected**                   Weak signals consistent with a
                                  particular state, insufficient to
                                  confirm. Shapes what CorpStage looks
                                  for. Does not drive action
                                  recommendations.

  **Inferred**                    Conclusion through reasoning across
                                  related intelligence elements. Labels
                                  clearly as inference with confidence
                                  score. Never presented as confirmed
                                  fact.

  **Partially Confirmed**         Some evidence supports the element,
                                  gaps remain. Actionable for
                                  lower-stakes decisions. Shows what
                                  would move this to Confirmed.

  **Confirmed**                   Known with high confidence from one or
                                  more reliable sources. Drives action
                                  recommendations. Presented without
                                  hedging unless source limitations
                                  exist.

  **Evidenced**                   Confirmed and supported by documentary
                                  evidence --- a contract, a filing, a
                                  verified measurement. The gold standard
                                  for board reporting and legal
                                  proceedings.

  **Stale**                       Was confirmed or evidenced previously,
                                  but reliability has degraded. Flagged
                                  visibly with age and typical decay
                                  rate. Triggers automatic refresh
                                  attempt. Never silently treated as
                                  current.

  **Contradicted**                Two or more credible sources give
                                  conflicting information. Active alert
                                  state. Both positions shown with
                                  sources. System does not choose.
                                  Escalates if unresolved.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**2.8 --- Enterprise Time Model**

Most intelligence systems understand current state. CorpStage
understands four temporal dimensions simultaneously --- because the most
important executive questions span all four.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Time Dimension**              **What it captures and why it matters**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Past --- Institutional        What has happened, what was decided,
  Memory**                        what was learned. Decision history with
                                  context, evidence, and outcome.
                                  Commitment history --- what was
                                  promised, when, whether delivered, at
                                  what variance. Leadership decision
                                  patterns. Strategic reversals.

  **Current --- Confirmed Present What is objectively true about the
  State**                         enterprise now from confirmed,
                                  high-confidence intelligence. The
                                  foundation --- but only one of four
                                  temporal dimensions. Treating it as the
                                  only one is the failure mode of every
                                  existing enterprise intelligence
                                  system.

  **Trajectory --- Rate and       How fast is the enterprise moving, in
  Direction**                     which direction, on each material
                                  dimension? Trajectory is more important
                                  than position. An enterprise at 40% of
                                  target but accelerating has a
                                  fundamentally different outlook than
                                  one at 70% but decelerating.

  **Future Exposure ---           What the enterprise will face from
  Probabilistic Range**           forces outside its immediate control.
                                  Regulatory pipeline --- what will
                                  become mandatory, when, at what cost?
                                  Physical climate trajectory over 5, 15,
                                  and 30-year horizons. Commitment
                                  maturity --- when do commitments come
                                  due and at what delivery probability?
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**2.9 --- Enterprise Value Translation Model**

Every piece of intelligence CorpStage holds must ultimately answer:
\"What does this mean for the value and resilience of my business?\"
Seven translation targets are defined.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Translation Target**          **What it measures and how CorpStage
                                  translates it**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **EBITDA Impact**               Direct effect on earnings. Primary
                                  translation for operational and cost
                                  intelligence. Point estimate plus
                                  range. Probability-weighted where
                                  impact is uncertain. Separated into
                                  impact already in current performance
                                  vs impact not yet in current numbers.

  **Revenue Consequence**         Effect on ability to generate revenue
                                  from customer changes, market access
                                  changes, and competitive position
                                  shifts. Revenue at risk by customer,
                                  contract, or segment. Separated by time
                                  horizon.

  **Resilience Value**            Contribution to or reduction of
                                  capacity to withstand stress without
                                  permanent value loss. Scenario-based
                                  --- the difference in enterprise
                                  outcomes between a resilient and a
                                  non-resilient enterprise in a defined
                                  adverse scenario.

  **Cost Exposure**               Total financial obligation from
                                  regulatory compliance, remediation,
                                  penalty risks, and litigation.
                                  Probability-weighted present value,
                                  separated by certainty level and timing
                                  horizon.

  **Financing Consequence**       Effect on access to capital, cost of
                                  capital, and capital structure
                                  flexibility. Basis point change in cost
                                  of debt for a defined positioning
                                  change. Green finance window ---
                                  estimated savings from better
                                  performance, in basis points and
                                  absolute currency.

  **Competitiveness**             Effect on relative competitive position
                                  --- winning customers, attracting
                                  talent, maintaining pricing power.
                                  Relative position against a defined
                                  peer group expressed as a percentile.

  **Enterprise Value**            Ultimate long-horizon translation ---
                                  effect on total equity value.
                                  Discounted cash flow sensitivity to key
                                  assumptions underlying the signal.
                                  Multiple change under different
                                  scenarios.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**2.10 --- Executive Relevance Model**

Everything CorpStage understands cannot and should not reach the
executive simultaneously. The Executive Relevance Model is the filter.
It answers one question before any intelligence is surfaced:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  ***\"Why should this specific executive care about this, right
  now?\"***
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Relevance Test**              **Criteria**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Test 1 --- Decision           Does this intelligence enable or
  Relevance**                     improve a decision the executive must
                                  make within their planning horizon? The
                                  decision it enables must be named
                                  before the intelligence is surfaced.

  **Test 2 --- Exception          Does this signal represent a meaningful
  Relevance**                     deviation from expected performance,
                                  committed trajectory, or normal
                                  operating parameters? Intelligence
                                  confirming what is expected has low
                                  relevance. Intelligence signalling
                                  deviation has high relevance.

  **Test 3 --- Timing Relevance** Is the executive\'s window to act on
                                  this intelligence open? Intelligence
                                  the executive cannot act on has low
                                  relevance regardless of its inherent
                                  importance.

  **Test 4 --- Authority          Does this intelligence require a
  Relevance**                     response that only this executive can
                                  authorise? If the appropriate response
                                  is within delegated authority, route to
                                  the right operational owner.

  **Test 5 --- Financial          Does this intelligence have a financial
  Relevance**                     consequence above the materiality
                                  threshold for this enterprise?
                                  Below-threshold signals are managed at
                                  operational level.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The Relevance Score drives the Action Center ranking --- not the
severity of the underlying signal, not the framework importance, not the
recency. This is how CorpStage maintains the maximum-7-items discipline
while holding a complete intelligence picture of the enterprise.

**2.11 --- The Enterprise Intelligence Lens Model**

CorpStage holds one intelligence model. One data layer. One IDAL. One
set of 16 understanding domains and 20 canonical intelligence objects.
One set of 12 canonical executive questions. What changes between roles
is not the data --- it is the vocabulary applied to it, the signals
foregrounded, and the outputs generated.

A lens is a presentation configuration that sits entirely above the
intelligence engine. Adding a new lens requires a vocabulary map and a
prioritisation configuration. It requires zero change to the
intelligence engine, the IDAL, the canonical questions, or the
understanding domains. The platform is infinitely lens-extensible by
design.

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Three Lenses at Launch**                                            |
|                                                                       |
| Lens 1 --- Executive / Financial Lens: CEO, CFO, COO, Board.          |
| Language: EBITDA impact, capital exposure, operational continuity,    |
| strategic commitment integrity. Section 14 Sacred 12 in full business |
| language.                                                             |
|                                                                       |
| Lens 2 --- Regulatory & Framework Detail Lens: CSO, Compliance &      |
| Reporting team, Compliance Analysts, Investor Relations. Language: BRSR, GRI, CSRD, ISSB S1/S2   |
| (absorbs TCFD), Scope 1/2/3, net zero trajectory. Same Sacred 12      |

| this lens only.                                                       |
|                                                                       |

| concentration risk, covenant breach risk, control failures. Same      |

| (Risk & Opportunity Center) becomes primary entry point.              |
+=======================================================================+

  **Adding a New Lens --- What It **Rule**
  Costs**                         
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Intelligence Engine Changes** None. Zero. IDAL, 16 Understanding

  **Database Changes**            One new row per term in
                                  LENS_VOCABULARY_MAP table. No
                                  structural database change.

  **Vocabulary Map Required**     A table: canonical term → lens-specific
                                  term. Approximately 40--60 translations
                                  per lens.

  **Prioritisation                Which Q domains and signals rank
  Configuration**                 highest for this role. A configuration
                                  --- not engineering.

  **Output Format**               Which document template is generated.
                                  Pre-built in the Regulatory Submission
                                  Engine.

  **Future Lenses Already         CPO Lens, IR Lens, Audit Committee
  Possible**                      Lens, Tax Lens, Treasury Lens --- all
                                  from Day One data. Two documents per
                                  new lens. One day of configuration.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The Lens Model means CorpStage is simultaneously the CFO\'s tool AND the
CSO\'s tool AND the CRO\'s tool. Three buyers. One platform. One source
of truth. See Law 39.

+========+=============================================================+
