The Canonical Intelligence Library defines the universe of intelligence
points CorpStage needs to understand a business. It is built on an
enterprise ontology --- not a framework ontology. Every intelligence
object holds: the intelligence point, its related data points,
cross-domain relationships, materiality weight, sourceability,
inferability, confidence model, refresh logic, stakeholder owner, and
framework mapping (hidden from executives).

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Architectural Distinction --- 20 Canonical Intelligence Domains vs  |
| 16 Understanding Domains (Step 2)**                                   |
|                                                                       |
| These 20 domains are DATA OBJECTS --- the specific intelligence       |
| points CorpStage collects, infers, and tracks.                        |
|                                                                       |
| The 16 Understanding Domains in Step 2 are the CONCEPTUAL MODEL       |
| within which these data objects live.                                 |
|                                                                       |
| A reader encountering 16 in Step 2 and 20 here is not seeing a        |
| contradiction --- these are different abstraction levels.             |
|                                                                       |
| The 16 are the lens. These 20 are what is seen through it. See also   |
| Section 2.11.                                                         |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **5.0a --- CIL Hierarchy Reconciliation (binding)**                   |
|                                                                       |
| The CIL Meta-Model (Doc 15.0) and this Step 5 architecture describe   |
| the same intelligence spine using two vocabularies developed at       |
| different times. They are reconciled, not contradictory. Three        |
| bindings apply:                                                       |
|                                                                       |
| > **1. CDE supersedes CDP --- same concept, refined name.**           |
| > "Canonical Data Element (CDE)" is the frozen name going forward for |
| > what Layer B below calls "Canonical Data Point (CDP)." The existing |
| > 245 data points (CDP-001 to CDP-245) are recast as CDEs without     |
| > renumbering or re-architecting. Existing CDP references elsewhere   |
| > in this document remain valid and synonymous with CDE; new work     |
| > should use CDE.                                                     |
| >                                                                     |
| > **2. Business Intelligence Requirement (BIR) is a new layer         |
| > inserted above the existing 70 Business Questions --- not a         |
| > replacement of them.** BQ-001 through BQ-070 (Layer A, below)       |
| > continue exactly as frozen --- same questions, same 7 workflow      |
| > buckets, same 15 industry override variants. Each now nests under   |
| > one BIR: a single sentence of business language stating what the    |
| > group of questions is collectively trying to establish (e.g. BIR:   |
| > "How is the enterprise organised legally and operationally?" groups |
| > the entity-structure questions within BQ-001--BQ-008). BIRs are     |
| > visible to executives; Business Questions are visible to the teams  |
| > answering them; CDEs remain system-facing and normally hidden ---   |
| > this visibility rule is unchanged.                                  |
| >                                                                     |
| > **3. Required / Recommended / Supplemental describes importance to  |
| > the Business Question --- never a mandate on the user.** This tier  |
| > (replacing the earlier Critical/Important/Optional language)        |
| > classifies whether a CDE can be skipped without weakening the       |
| > answer to its Business Question. It does not change acquisition     |
| > order. Discover → Infer → Validate → Ask (this document) and        |
| > Extract → Retrieve → Infer → Confirm → Route → Ask (Law 4) remain   |
| > the same sequence at different resolutions. A CDE marked "Required" |
| > is still discovered or inferred first; the user is asked only if    |
| > every prior stage fails --- regardless of importance tier.          |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **5.0b --- Intelligence Construction & Framework Reconciliation       |
| (binding)**                                                           |
|                                                                       |
| **Intelligence Construction Principle.** CorpStage does not collect   |
| data for frameworks --- it builds enterprise intelligence.            |
| Frameworks, reports, disclosures, assessments, and executive insights |
| are downstream consumers of that intelligence, never its purpose.     |
| This restates Law 2 and Law 25 (Invisible Compliance) at the          |
| data-construction level.                                              |
|                                                                       |
| **Extensibility confirmed.** A new Business Question requires only:   |
| one BQ nested under an existing (or new) BIR, plus 3--7 CDEs beneath  |
| it, some reused, some new. Domain, Intelligence Area, and BIR do not  |
| move. This is the same extensibility guarantee already frozen for     |
| Domains (Section 4 / Law 8 extensibility) applied one layer down ---  |
| BQ-071 onward requires zero change to IDAL, Confidence Architecture,  |
| Executive Questions, or the Sacred 12.                                |
|                                                                       |
| **Framework Reconciliation Principle --- composed, not replaced.**    |
| Framework → Business Question is the primary, human-visible           |
| reconciliation surface: a CSO or compliance lead configuring          |
| framework coverage reasons in terms of "which Business Questions does |
| this framework disclosure require," not in terms of individual CDEs.  |
| Framework → CDE remains the underlying mechanical mapping the         |
| extraction engine executes against (Layer B / Layer C, Step 5; the    |
| LENS_VOCABULARY_MAP and framework mapping tables already in schema).  |
| The two are consistent, not competing: a Business Question owns its   |
| CDEs, so mapping a framework question to a BQ implicitly reaches      |
| every CDE beneath it. Where a framework disclosure needs only some of |
| a BQ's CDEs --- not all --- the CDE-level mapping is the binding      |
| source of truth for extraction; the BQ-level mapping remains the      |
| binding surface for human configuration and the example below.        |
|                                                                       |
| > Example --- BRSR "List subsidiaries and associate entities" →       |
| > Business Question "What subsidiaries exist?" → BIR "How is the      |
| > enterprise organised legally and operationally?" → Domain:          |
| > Enterprise Intelligence. Underneath, the same BRSR question maps    |
| > mechanically to CDE-level fields --- Subsidiary Name, Country,      |
| > Ownership %, Status --- consistent with the CDP/CDE framework       |
| > mapping already frozen in Step 5 (e.g. CDP-060 mapping to           |
| > GRI/BRSR/ESRS/ISSB/CDP simultaneously).                             |
|                                                                       |
| **User Interaction Reconciliation.** Users are rarely asked a         |
| Business Question directly. Sequence: Discover (system finds the      |
| answer) → Infer (system estimates it) → Validate (system asks the     |
| user to confirm a finding) → Ask (system asks the Business Question   |
| outright, only if every prior stage fails). This is Law 4             |
| (Discover→Infer→Ask Last) restated at the Business Question level:    |
| instead of "What subsidiaries exist?" CorpStage opens with "We        |
| identified 12 subsidiaries from annual reports and corporate filings. |
| Confidence: 91%. Please confirm."                                     |
|                                                                       |
| **Reporting Reconciliation.** Reports are generated from answered     |
| Business Questions --- never from forms, questionnaires, or framework |
| templates directly. One answered Business Question (e.g. "Who owns    |
| Business Resilience governance?" → "Chief Resilience Officer") simultaneously     |
| satisfies every framework that maps to it --- BRSR, GRI, ISSB, ESRS,  |
| and internal reporting --- with zero duplicate collection. This is    |
| the same one-fact-many-frameworks model already frozen for CDP-060 in |
| Step 5, restated at the Business Question level per the CIL           |
| Meta-Model freeze (Doc 15.0, Sections 5 and 9).                       |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **5.0c --- Node Applicability & Framework Governance (binding)**      |
|                                                                       |
| A single CDE (e.g. Energy Consumption) is one canonical fact          |
| collected at different points in the G1 node hierarchy --- Plant,     |
| Site, Country, Company, Group --- and aggregated upward. A Framework  |
| (e.g. an EHS report scoped at Plant level, aggregated to Country)     |
| names which CDEs it needs and at which node level. Frameworks         |
| themselves are not all equal in who may create or change them. Eight  |
| bindings apply:                                                       |
|                                                                       |
| > **1. Node Applicability is a property of the CDE, defaulting to the |
| > highest defined node --- never asked, never blocking.** Every CDE   |
| > carries a Node Applicability attribute listing which G1 node types  |
| > it can legitimately be collected at. If the organisation has not    |
| > defined a multi-level hierarchy in G1 (Section 5.0a parent          |
| > reference), every CDE collapses to Company level automatically ---  |
| > the system never asks "which node?" when there is only one          |
| > meaningful answer. Where multiple nodes exist, the system infers    |
| > the correct node from context (the document being read, the         |
| > connected system's scope, the framework's stated scope) before ever |
| > asking the user to specify it --- consistent with Law 4 and the     |
| > Discover→Infer→Validate→Ask sequence (Doc 15.0, Section 2).         |
| > Aggregation upward through the hierarchy follows the Aggregation    |
| > Rule already defined per CDE (Section 5.0b CDE schema); node-level  |
| > collection does not introduce a second aggregation mechanism.       |
| >                                                                     |
| > **2. Three framework tiers, three governance owners --- never       |
| > two.**                                                              |
| >                                                                     |
| > **Tier 1 --- Standard Frameworks (CorpStage Admin only):** BRSR,    |
| > GRI, ISSB, ESRS, CDP and equivalents. Externally governed and       |
| > identical across every customer; if the regulator changes the       |
| > framework, CorpStage Admin changes it once, centrally. No Corporate |
| > Admin may edit, fork, or silently diverge a Standard Framework ---  |
| > doing so would break the "one fact, many consumers" guarantee       |
| > (Section 5.0b, Reporting Reconciliation) for every other customer   |
| > relying on the same canonical mapping.                              |
| >                                                                     |
| > **Tier 2 --- Custom Frameworks (Corporate Admin):** Fully bespoke,  |
| > built from scratch, owned entirely by one customer, never shared,   |
| > never affecting any other instance. Example: an internal Financial  |
| > Reporting Framework a CFO team builds for the CEO and Board. The    |
| > Corporate Admin selects existing CDEs where they match and creates  |
| > new ones only where no match exists (Binding 3).                    |
| >                                                                     |
| > **Tier 3 --- Extended Frameworks (Corporate Admin, additive         |
| > only):** A Corporate Admin may clone a Standard Framework into      |
| > their own namespace and add to it (e.g. "BRSR plus three internal   |
| > board questions"). The clone inherits every Standard mapping; the   |
| > Corporate Admin may add new Business Questions and CDEs on top, but |
| > may never delete, redefine, or override an inherited Standard       |
| > mapping. This is the tier that prevents Tier 2 from being used as a |
| > workaround to silently fork a Standard Framework one customer at a  |
| > time.                                                               |
| >                                                                     |
| > **3. CDEs are Global or Corporate-Scoped --- net-new CDEs default   |
| > to Corporate-Scoped; promotion to Global is a CorpStage Admin       |
| > decision, never automatic.** When a Corporate Admin needs a CDE     |
| > that does not yet exist (Tier 2 or Tier 3), the platform first      |
| > attempts a semantic match against the existing Global CDE library   |
| > (e.g. a proposed "Net Revenue" CDE should be offered the existing   |
| > "Revenue" CDE as a likely match) --- preventing silent duplication  |
| > of the same underlying fact under a different name. If no match     |
| > exists, the new CDE is created Corporate-Scoped: visible and usable |
| > only within that customer's instance, fully subject to the same     |
| > schema (Validation Rule, Temporal, Cardinality, Aggregation Rule,   |
| > System of Record --- Section 5.0b CDE schema) as every Global CDE.  |
| > If multiple customers independently create the materially same      |
| > Corporate-Scoped CDE, this is read as a signal --- not an automatic |
| > trigger --- that a new Global CDE, and potentially a new Business   |
| > Question or Domain, may be needed; CorpStage Admin reviews and      |
| > decides whether to promote it.                                      |
| >                                                                     |
| > **4. An unrecognised future framework is onboarded through the same |
| > Extract→Infer→Confirm pipeline as any other document --- never a    |
| > manual architect-only process.** When a user names a framework      |
| > CorpStage does not yet recognise, its disclosure list or            |
| > requirements document is ingested exactly as any other uploaded     |
| > document (Section 7.9 Intelligence Intake Guardrails apply          |
| > identically). The platform attempts to semantically match each      |
| > disclosure to an existing Business Question first, and to an        |
| > existing CDE beneath it second --- reusing Binding 3's matching     |
| > mechanism. Disclosures with no match become new Business Question   |
| > candidates, surfaced to a human (the Corporate Admin for a Tier 2/3 |
| > framework; CorpStage Admin if the framework is later proposed for   |
| > Tier 1 promotion) for a one-time confirmation before the framework  |
| > becomes active. From that point forward, the framework operates     |
| > identically to any other --- Framework→Business Question is the     |
| > visible mapping, Framework→CDE is the underlying mechanical one     |
| > (Section 5.0b), and reporting from it is fully automated and        |
| > invisible per Law 25.                                               |
| >                                                                     |
| > **5. An extracted fact with no matching CDE is never discarded ---  |
| > it is captured to the Unclassified Intelligence Registry and held   |
| > until a human resolves it.** Category 5 (Section 7.9) already       |
| > routes content the platform cannot map to any of the 20 Domains to  |
| > Unclassified Intelligence for Governance Manager review. This       |
| > binding extends the same protection one level deeper: the far more  |
| > common case where the Domain and likely Business Question are       |
| > obvious, but no Canonical Data Element yet exists to hold the       |
| > specific fact extracted. The platform never discards the fact and   |
| > never forces it into the nearest wrong CDE. Instead it is written   |
| > to the Unclassified Intelligence Registry (Doc 15.x, platform-level |
| > --- not per-domain, since the gap is in the schema, not the data)   |
| > with, at minimum: the raw extracted value; the source document,     |
| > page or section, and extraction method (Section 5.0b, Evidence      |
| > Accessibility); the LLM's best-guess label for what the fact        |
| > represents; and an extraction confidence score distinct from any    |
| > CDE-level confidence score, since no CDE exists yet to carry one. A |
| > Governance Manager subsequently does exactly one of three things:   |
| > map the entry to an existing CDE the automated semantic match       |
| > missed; confirm it is genuinely new and create a CDE for it,        |
| > Corporate-Scoped by default per Binding 3; or mark it not relevant  |
| > and discard. If the materially same entry recurs independently      |
| > across multiple customers' registries, this feeds the same          |
| > promotion signal as Binding 3 --- evidence that a Global CDE is     |
| > missing, surfaced to CorpStage Admin, never auto-created.           |
| >                                                                     |
| > **6. Every CDE has exactly one owning Domain, regardless of how     |
| > many Domains consume it --- ownership goes to where the fact is     |
| > most naturally extracted and validated, never to every Domain that  |
| > finds it useful.** Section 5 already establishes that one fact may  |
| > feed many Domains (e.g. Supplier data feeding Supply Chain, Risk,   |
| > Financial, and Operational Intelligence simultaneously) --- that is |
| > consumption, and remains unchanged. This binding addresses a        |
| > different question Section 5 does not answer: which Domain holds    |
| > the canonical CDE record itself. A boundary-spanning fact (e.g. a   |
| > Data Protection Officer's name, which Enterprise Intelligence could |
| > plausibly hold as a governance role and Cyber & Information         |
| > Security Intelligence could plausibly hold as a compliance contact) |
| > is assigned a single owning Domain using this order of precedence:  |
| > (a) the Domain whose Evidence Source most directly produces the     |
| > fact (Section 5.0b CDE schema, Default Evidence Source) --- a fact  |
| > extracted from the Annual Report's governance section is owned by   |
| > Enterprise Intelligence even if a Cyber domain consumes it; (b)     |
| > where Evidence Source is ambiguous between Domains, the Domain      |
| > whose Business Questions the fact most directly answers (Section    |
| > 5.0a, BQ definition); (c) where (a) and (b) both remain genuinely   |
| > tied, CorpStage Admin makes a one-time ownership ruling, recorded   |
| > against the CDE, binding on all Domains thereafter. Every other     |
| > Domain references the owning Domain's CDE rather than creating its  |
| > own --- this is the same "one fact, many consumers" guarantee       |
| > already frozen in Section 5.0b, applied at the point of CDE         |
| > creation rather than only at the point of framework mapping. A      |
| > CDE's Domain ownership is recorded explicitly in the CDE schema and |
| > is visible to any Domain architect before they create a CDE that    |
| > might already exist elsewhere --- preventing the duplication this   |
| > binding exists to close. \*\*7. Hide and Purge are two distinct,    |
| > separately governed actions on a data element --- never conflated,  |
| > never interchangeable.\*\* A data element a department or role does |
| > not wish to see in its default view is Hidden, not Purged, and the  |
| > two carry materially different consequences. Hide: reversible,      |
| > role- or department-scoped, requires no approval and no audit entry |
| > beyond the standard activity log. A Hidden CDE's historic values,   |
| > evidence lineage, and confidence scores are fully preserved and     |
| > remain visible to any other department, role, or framework that     |
| > legitimately consumes the same fact (consistent with the "one fact, |
| > many consumers" guarantee, Section 5.0b) --- Hiding affects only    |
| > the requesting view, never the underlying canonical record. A user  |
| > may un-hide a previously hidden element at any time without         |
| > approval. Purge: a controlled soft-deletion, never a hard delete,   |
| > reserved for data elements no longer relevant to any department,    |
| > role, or framework --- for example a Corporate-Scoped CDE created   |
| > in error, or a Temporary CDE (Binding 3) whose business need has    |
| > lapsed. Purge requires Corporate Admin approval, is recorded        |
| > permanently in the audit trail (requestor, approver, timestamp, and |
| > reason --- consistent with the audit standard already set for       |
| > conflict resolution, Section 7.9 Category 7), and the underlying    |
| > record, evidence, and historic values are retained in an inactive   |
| > state, never destroyed --- satisfying Law 13 (Defensibility by      |
| > Design) and the regulatory retention obligations a genuinely        |
| > deleted record could not satisfy. A Purged element cannot be        |
| > un-purged by the requesting user; restoration requires the same     |
| > Corporate Admin approval as the original Purge. Neither Hide nor    |
| > Purge ever removes a CDE from the Global canonical library --- both |
| > actions operate only at the Corporate-Scoped or view-configuration  |
| > layer (Binding 3); a Global CDE's presence in the canonical model   |
| > is a CorpStage Admin decision exclusively, consistent with Binding  |
| > 3's promotion-only-on-review rule applied in reverse. \*\*8.        |
| > Framework Completeness is a derived percentage, never a stored      |
| > value --- computed from Business Questions answered, not data       |
| > points counted.\*\* A Framework's Completeness = (number of that    |
| > Framework's mapped Business Questions with a Confirmed or           |
| > Verified-confidence answer, per Section 5.0b's Framework→Business   |
| > Question reconciliation surface) ÷ (total Business Questions that   |
| > Framework requires). This is deliberately a Business Question       |
| > ratio, not a CDE ratio: a single answered Business Question can     |
| > satisfy several CDEs at once (Section 5.0b, Reporting               |
| > Reconciliation), so counting at the CDE level would understate true |
| > completeness and re-surface CDE-level mechanics the executive       |
| > should never see (Law 22, Protect Executive Cognition from Noise).  |
| > This is distinct from, and must never be confused with, Domain      |
| > Completeness (the domain-level "what do we know about this company  |
| > today" view, Section 5.0e below) --- Domain Completeness describes  |
| > the organisation's overall knowledge state with no fixed            |
| > denominator; Framework Completeness describes one specific          |
| > Framework's defined requirement against that same knowledge state.  |
| > The same organisation can be 40% complete against IFRS and 85%      |
| > complete against BRSR simultaneously, computed from the identical   |
| > underlying CDE pool, because the two Frameworks require different,  |
| > overlapping subsets of it.                                          |
| >                                                                     |
| > Binding 3 (CDE Scope) describes Global promotion as CorpStage Admin |
| > observing convergence across customers and initiating the review. A |
| > Corporate Admin may also actively request promotion of their own    |
| > Corporate-Scoped CDE --- for example, to share it with a separate   |
| > instance of their own group, or because they believe it has broader |
| > value. The request follows the identical review: semantic-match     |
| > check against the existing Global library, then a CorpStage Admin   |
| > decision. A request is never auto-approved regardless of who        |
| > initiates it; the only difference between the two promotion paths   |
| > is who raises the question, not how it is resolved.                 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **5.0d --- Department, Role, and View Extensibility (binding)**       |
|                                                                       |
| Departments (Finance, HR, Supply Chain, Risk, Legal, and any future   |
| addition) and Executive Roles (CFO, CHRO, CRO, and any future         |
| addition) are platform metadata, not hardcoded application logic ---  |
| consistent with the same extensibility principle already frozen for   |
| Domains (Section 4 / Law 8) and Frameworks (Section 5.0c, Binding 2). |
| A department or role is a named record carrying: a default visibility |
| configuration (which CDEs/Domains are shown by default, subject to    |
| Hide per Section 5.0c Binding 7), an aggregation rule for role-level  |
| views (Binding 2 below), and --- for roles specifically --- a Lens    |
| assignment (Section 2.11) determining the vocabulary the role sees.   |
| **1. CorpStage Admin may add a new Department or Role without         |
| engineering change.** Adding "Chief AI Officer" or "Biodiversity"     |
| follows the identical pattern already frozen for adding a new Lens    |
| (Section 2.11, ⚑ NEW LAW --- Infinite Extensibility): a new metadata  |
| record, not a new code path. No change to the intelligence engine,    |
| the IDAL, the Canonical Intelligence Library, or any existing         |
| department's or role's configuration. **2. A Role View is an          |
| aggregation of Department Views, configured once, computed always.**  |
| A CFO's view is not a separately maintained dataset --- it is the     |
| union of the Finance, Risk, and Supply Chain department views (or     |
| whichever departments the role's configuration names), recomputed     |
| live from each department's current visibility configuration.         |
| Changing what Finance hides or shows automatically and immediately    |
| changes what the CFO sees, with zero separate maintenance --- the     |
| same "configure once, compute always" principle already governing     |
| Framework→BQ→CDE reconciliation (Section 5.0b). **3. Department and   |
| Role view configuration is independent of, and does not alter, CDE    |
| ownership.** A Department or Role choosing to hide or surface a CDE   |
| (Section 5.0c Binding 7) changes only what that audience sees --- it  |
| never changes the CDE's owning Domain (Section 5.0c, Binding 6), its  |
| Global or Corporate-Scoped status (Binding 3), or its presence in any |
| other Department's or Role's view. View configuration is              |
| presentation-layer metadata; CDE ownership and scope remain canonical |
| and unaffected by it.                                                 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **5.0e --- Domain Coverage Dashboard (operational layer, not Sacred   |
| 12)**                                                                 |
|                                                                       |
| Purpose: shows what CorpStage currently knows about this specific     |
| organisation in one Domain --- never what it is required to know      |
| (that is Framework Completeness, Section 5.0c Binding 8, a different  |
| metric entirely). This is operational-team-facing data-acquisition    |
| surface, not a Sacred 12 / Executive Business Question surface ---    |
| per Law 40 (Executive Cognition Separation), a Domain Business        |
| Question screen must never be conflated with or repurposed as an      |
| executive screen, and this dashboard must not be presented on, or     |
| merged with, any Sacred 12 screen. Displays, per Domain: **Total Data |
| Elements Found** (the count of CDEs with at least one value of any    |
| confidence level for this organisation) · **Discovered** (IDAL Stage  |
| 1/2, no human input) · **Inferred** (IDAL Stage 3, no human           |
| confirmation yet) · **Confirmed** (IDAL Stage 4/5, human-validated) · |
| **Pending Review** (in the Intelligent Work Routing Engine queue,     |
| Stage 5a). This dashboard has no fixed denominator and must never     |
| imply one --- a Domain's card never states a required total (e.g.     |
| "Finance Domain = 300 mandatory data points"); fixed requirements     |
| exist only at the Framework level (Section 5.0c Binding 8), never at  |
| the Domain level. Where a Department or Role has Hidden certain CDEs  |
| (Section 5.0c Binding 7), the dashboard counts reflect only the       |
| visible subset for that viewer --- Hidden elements are excluded from  |
| the displayed total but remain in the underlying canonical count used |
| for Framework Completeness, since Hiding is a presentation action and |
| never alters the canonical record (Binding 7).                        |

**5.1 --- Three-Layer Data Architecture**

CorpStage operates on a three-layer data architecture. Every piece of
intelligence passes through all three layers. Executives see only the
top. Framework compliance emerges invisibly from the bottom. This
architecture is the single-source-of-truth model that makes the Lens
Principle (Law 39) possible.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Layer**                       **Definition and Contents**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Layer A --- Business          70 business questions written in plain
  Questions (User-Facing)**       operational language. Grouped in 7
                                  workflow buckets. Industry-specific
                                  phrasings for 15 industries (105
                                  override variants). These are what
                                  teams answer to populate the
                                  intelligence engine. These are NOT the
                                  12 canonical executive questions ---
                                  those are the executive cognition layer
                                  above. BQ-001 through BQ-070. Each
                                  business question resolves to 3--7
                                  canonical data points (Layer B).
                                  Sequenced in 7 UX phases: Foundation
                                  first, Optional last.

  **Layer B --- Canonical Data    245 normalised, framework-agnostic data
  Points (Intelligence Engine)**  points. CDP-001 through CDP-245. These
                                  are the atomic units of truth. Each
                                  data point is unique, unambiguous, and
                                  mappable to multiple frameworks
                                  simultaneously. CDP-060 (Direct Cost
                                  emissions) maps to GRI 305-1, BRSR
                                  P6-E6, ESRS E1-6, ISSB S2-10, CDP C6.1,
                                  DJSI CSA-ENV-2, California SB-253,
                                  Australia ASRS simultaneously. These
                                  ARE the intelligence objects in the
                                  Canonical Intelligence Library. The 20
                                  library domains organise them. The 245
                                  data points are the specific items
                                  within those domains.

  **Layer C --- Framework         368 framework disclosure requirements
  Disclosures (Invisible          across 20 frameworks. GRI 2021, BRSR
  Backend)**                      Comprehensive, BRSR Core (9
                                  attributes), ESRS post-Omnibus I
                                  December 2025 (simplified --- 27
                                  disclosures, 61% reduction from
                                  original), ISSB IFRS S1+S2 (absorbs
                                  TCFD which disbanded October 2023), CDP
                                  2026, SASB-ISSB, UNGC 2025/26, DJSI/S&P
                                  CSA 2024, EU Taxonomy post-Omnibus,
                                  CSDDD post-Omnibus, CBAM definitive
                                  period January 2026, TNFD v1.0,
                                  California SB-253/261, Australia ASRS,
                                  Modern Slavery Acts, EcoVadis, PCAF,
                                  SBTi. Never visible to any executive.
                                  Visible only in Regulatory & Framework Detail Lens for
                                  CSO and Compliance & Reporting team users.

**Industry Override Principle**

The same 70 business questions are rephrased for 15 industries. The
underlying canonical data point (Layer B) is identical. Only the
question language changes. G1 Organisation Setup captures the industry
--- this selection determines which question phrasings the user sees
throughout the platform. Current industries covered: Apparel & Textiles,
Automotive, Banking & Financial Services, Chemicals, Construction & Real
Estate, Consumer Goods, Energy & Utilities, Food & Agriculture,
Healthcare & Pharma, Mining & Metals, Oil & Gas, Retail, Technology,
Telecommunications, Transport & Logistics.

**6.1 --- The 70 Business Questions: 7 Workflow Buckets**

The 70 business questions (Layer A) are grouped into 7 workflow buckets.
Each bucket maps to specific Q domains and business domains. These are
what functional teams answer to populate the intelligence engine. They
are written in plain operational language --- never framework language.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

**6.2 --- Question Layers and Interaction Model**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Question Layer**              **Purpose and examples**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Layer 1 --- Enterprise        Understand business context. Low
  Understanding**                 frequency. Examples: \"What are your
                                  primary sources of revenue?\" · \"Which
                                  regions matter most operationally?\" ·
                                  \"Which suppliers are hardest to
                                  replace?\"

  **Layer 2 --- Intelligence      Close confidence gaps. High-value asks
  Completion**                    only. \"We understand your
                                  manufacturing footprint but are less
                                  certain about waste disposal practices.
                                  Spend 2 minutes to improve Supplier
                                  Continuity Intelligence and Operational
                                  Risk assessment --- protecting an
                                  estimated ₹30Cr operational exposure.\"

  **Layer 3 --- Contradiction     Resolve inconsistency. \"Annual report
  Resolution**                    suggests renewable transition priority.
                                  Operations indicate diesel reliance
                                  increasing. Has operating reality
                                  changed since strategic commitments
                                  were made?\"

  **Layer 4 --- Executive         Power Sacred 12 Screens. Cognitive
  Reflection**                    inquiry, not data collection. \"Which
                                  priorities receive funding even under
                                  pressure?\"

  **Layer 5 --- Scenario**        Support simulations. \"If a major
                                  supplier disruption occurred, which
                                  operations would be affected first?\"
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Question Principle**          **Rule**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Suppression Logic**           Do NOT ask if: already extracted ·
                                  retrieved externally · inferred
                                  confidently · previously confirmed ·
                                  immaterial. Preserves calm executive
                                  experience.

  **Ordering Logic**              Prioritise by: Materiality × Financial
                                  Impact × Confidence Gap × Urgency ×
                                  Executive Relevance × Cross-Domain
                                  Impact × Contradiction Severity × Ease
                                  of Resolution (see Step 12.3 ---
                                  authoritative formula).

  **Framing Model**               Questions must always feel:
                                  business-first · intelligent ·
                                  respectful · minimal · premium. Never:
                                  compliance burden.

  **Guided Completion**           Always declare value before asking.
                                  \"Spend 3 minutes → Regulatory Cost
                                  Exposure assessment improves 18%. Also
                                  improves: Supplier Intelligence ·
                                  Operational Risk modelling.\"
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

underlying canonical data point (Layer B) is identical --- only the
question language changes. G1 Organisation Setup captures the industry
at onboarding. That selection drives all question phrasings throughout
the platform.

| **Step | **Intelligent Data Acquisition Architecture (IDAL)**        |
| 7**    |                                                             |
|        | *How CorpStage acquires enterprise truth. Understand first. |
|        | Ask last.*                                                  |
+========+=============================================================+
+--------+-------------------------------------------------------------+

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **IDAL Core Philosophy**                                              |
|                                                                       |
| Wrong enterprise model: Collect → Validate → Report                   |
|                                                                       |
| CorpStage model: Understand → Infer → Confirm → Strengthen Confidence |
|                                                                       |
| The burden of understanding belongs to the system. Humans only        |
| resolve what the system cannot know.                                  |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **IDAL Stage**                  **Purpose, sources, and principle**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Stage 1 --- EXTRACT**         Acquire deterministic truth. Sources:
                                  ERP, Finance systems, HRMS,
                                  Procurement, CRM, EHS, Operations,
                                  Energy systems, uploaded evidence,
                                  annual reports, policies, contracts,
                                  invoices, utility bills, board minutes.
                                  Techniques: OCR, NLP, table extraction,
                                  entity extraction, semantic parsing.
                                  Principle: Deterministic truth first.

  **Stage 2 --- RETRIEVE**        Acquire contextual truth. See Section
                                  7.1 (Intelligence Sources) for full
                                  specification of all external sources.
                                  Principle: Enterprise truth exists
                                  outside the enterprise too.

  **Stage 3 --- INFER**           Reduce uncertainty intelligently.
                                  Types: Deterministic inference,
                                  Benchmark inference (peer comparison),
                                  Pattern inference (historical
                                  behaviour), Relationship inference
                                  (cross-signal reasoning), Behavioural
                                  inference (commitment patterns →
                                  execution fragility). Principle: Infer
                                  aggressively, assert conservatively.

  **Stage 4 --- CONFIRM**         Fast confidence improvement. Preferred
                                  human interaction. \"We believe energy
                                  costs increased primarily due to
                                  production growth. Correct?\" --- Yes /
                                  Modify. Not: \"Enter energy
                                  information.\" Principle: Confirmation
                                  over entry.

  **Stage 5 --- CORRECT**         Improve inferred truth. \"We identified
                                  14 strategic suppliers. 3 may be harder
                                  to replace. Correct if needed.\"
                                  Principle: Refinement before manual
                                  entry.

  **Stage 5a --- ROUTE (NEW       Intelligent Work Routing Engine. Every
  v2.1)**                         intelligence element that cannot be
                                  auto-resolved is immediately allocated
                                  to the closest domain owner based on
                                  domain ownership table + materiality
                                  score + confidence gap. Owner options:
                                  Confirm / Correct / Delegate (once
                                  only). If unresolved within resolution
                                  window: escalates to functional head →
                                  then surfaces on Executive Home as a
                                  named financial exposure gap. High
                                  materiality: 48-hour window. Medium: 7
                                  days. Low: 30 days. No intelligence
                                  element is ever unattended. No gap is
                                  ever unowned. See Law 8 and
                                  INTELLIGENCE_WORK_QUEUE database table.

  **Stage 6 --- ASK**             Only unresolved truth. Only when:
                                  cannot extract AND cannot retrieve AND
                                  cannot infer AND confidence inadequate
                                  AND materiality high AND routing has
                                  not resolved it. Examples: \"Which
                                  priorities remain protected during cost
                                  pressure?\" Principle: Ask only what
                                  humans uniquely know. Stage 5a ensures
                                  this stage is genuinely rare.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **IDAL Component**              **Definition**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Determinism Framework**       Every intelligence point classified as:
                                  Deterministic (system acts) ·
                                  Probabilistic (infer + confirm) ·
                                  Ambiguous (system asks) · Strategic
                                  (human-in-loop mandatory).

  **Confidence Propagation**      New intelligence affects related
                                  intelligence. Supplier confirmation
                                  improves: Operational Risk confidence,
                                  Financial Exposure modelling, Supplier
                                  Resilience assessment, Regulatory Cost
                                  Exposure. Huge leverage.

  **Contradiction Detection**     System detects: document says renewable
                                  priority / spend data says fossil
                                  increase → triggers contradiction
                                  workflow before assuming truth.

  **Human-in-the-Loop Gates**     Mandatory for: executive narratives ·
                                  strategic assumptions · financial
                                  materiality · board outputs ·
                                  contradictory intelligence ·
                                  low-confidence inference.

**7.9 --- Intelligence Intake Guardrails**

*Every document, file, or connection entering CorpStage through Stage 1
(Extract) passes through a guardrail layer before becoming intelligence.
The governing principle is binding: warn, never silently fail; block
only for security and integrity. Everything else is surfaced to the
human for a decision --- never silently rejected, never silently
accepted.*

  ----------------- -----------------------------------------------------
  **Category 1 ---  Same filename → warn, ask whether to proceed (may be
  Duplicate         an update). Same content (hash match) → block, exact
  Prevention**      duplicate already exists. Same document type and
                    period but different content → flag as version
                    conflict; ask to replace or keep both. Superseded
                    documents are never deleted --- retained in history,
                    marked superseded.

  **Category 2 ---  Corrupt or unparseable file → reject with reason.
  File Integrity**  Password-protected or encrypted → reject, ask user to
                    remove protection and re-upload. Zero-byte file →
                    reject. Partially uploaded file → do not process; ask
                    for re-upload. These are hard blocks --- no
                    exceptions.

  **Category 3 ---  Supported: PDF, DOCX, XLSX/XLS, PPTX, CSV, plain
  File Type**       text, images (with OCR), email formats (MSG, EML).
                    Unsupported: executables, compressed archives (unless
                    unpackable), audio, video --- reject with reason and
                    list of supported formats. Disguised files (wrong
                    extension for actual content) → reject.

  **Category 4 ---  Maximum 200MB per file --- reject above this with a
  File Size**       suggestion to split the file. Maximum 1GB per upload
                    batch --- excess files queued for sequential
                    processing. Minimum 1KB --- warn (likely empty or
                    test file) but do not block.

  **Category 5 ---  Zero intelligence extracted → flag as "Low yield"
  Content           with explanation (scanned image without OCR,
  Relevance**       non-business content, or outside current domain
                    coverage). Items the platform cannot confidently map
                    to any of the 20 domains are not discarded --- they
                    are routed to the Unclassified Intelligence domain
                    for Governance Manager review and assignment.
                    Personal documents (passport, personal tax return) →
                    warn before processing. Document appears to belong to
                    a different organisation → warn and ask for
                    confirmation.

  **Category 6 ---  Virus or malware detected → hard block, no content
  Security &        stored, no exceptions. PII pattern detected (Aadhaar,
  Compliance**      PAN, passport, credit card numbers) → warn before
                    processing and require confirmation. Confidentiality
                    markings ("Strictly Confidential", "Board Only") →
                    accept, restrict access to authorised roles, notify
                    the Governance Manager. Regulatory restrictions (e.g.
                    unpublished price-sensitive information) → flag and
                    route to Governance Manager for an access-control
                    decision before the content becomes visible to any
                    other user.

  **Category 7 ---  Document period does not match the configured
  Organisational    reporting period → warn (historical reference or
  Integrity**       error?). Document appears to belong to a different
                    node in the organisation hierarchy → warn and offer
                    to reassign. Extracted data conflicts with existing
                    Verified-confidence data → surfaced as a conflict
                    card for human resolution --- never auto-overwritten.
                    The resolution, the value chosen, the value
                    superseded, the resolver's identity, and the
                    timestamp are recorded permanently in the audit
                    trail. Update affects aggregation across multiple
                    parent nodes → warn before applying.

  **Category 8 ---  Maximum 20 files per upload session --- beyond this,
  User Behaviour**  ask for confirmation before proceeding. More than 50
                    files uploaded by one user within one hour → flag for
                    admin review (possible automation or error). Every
                    upload attempt --- successful, rejected, or warned
                    --- is recorded in the audit trail with filename,
                    timestamp, uploader identity, and the reason if
                    rejected or warned.
  ----------------- -----------------------------------------------------

***Governing principle:** warn, never silently fail. Block only for
security and integrity (Categories 2 and 6). Every other guardrail
surfaces a decision to the human --- consistent with Law 18
(Recommendation Never Decision) and Law 4 (Confirm before Ask).*

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Foundational Principle**                                            |
|                                                                       |
| CorpStage never claims certainty it cannot defend.                    |
|                                                                       |
| Everything must answer: \"Why should I trust this?\"                  |
|                                                                       |
| Every intelligence point has: Origin · Evidence · Confidence ·        |
| Explainability · Traceability · Freshness · Contradiction Status ·    |
| Human Validation Status. Trust is engineered.                         |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

**Confidence Scale (0--100%)**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Score Range** **Meaning**
  --------------- -------------------------------------------------------
  **0--20%**      Unknown

  **21--40%**     Weak inference

  **41--60%**     Directional confidence

  **61--80%**     Operationally reliable

  **81--95%**     High confidence

  **96--100%**    Deterministic / verified
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

Important: confidence ≠ correctness. It means defensibility of belief. A
wrong confident assertion destroys trust permanently. Appropriate
uncertainty earns more trust than false precision.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Confidence Input**            **How it affects the confidence score**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **A. Source Reliability**       ERP Finance: High · Manual estimate:
                                  Medium · Web inference: Variable ·
                                  Supplier declaration: Medium-high ·
                                  Audited report: High.

  **B. Evidence Strength**        Weak: statement · Medium: uploaded
                                  document · Strong: audited evidence ·
                                  Very Strong: multiple corroborated
                                  sources.

  **C. Consistency**              Annual report: renewable transition /
                                  Spend: diesel increase → confidence
                                  reduced. Contradictory evidence weakens
                                  confidence materially.

  **D. Freshness**                Older information decays confidence.
                                  CorpStage applies decay functions by
                                  intelligence type. Regulatory signals
                                  decay fastest. Strategic signals decay
                                  slowest.

  **E. Human Confirmation**       Confirmed by stakeholder → confidence
                                  increases. Overridden by stakeholder →
                                  confidence recalibrates to human input.

  **F. Cross-Signal Validation**  Multiple signals supporting the same
                                  truth → stronger confidence.
                                  Procurement + invoices + supplier
                                  contracts all corroborating the same
                                  fact.

  **G. Materiality Sensitivity**  Higher materiality → higher confidence
                                  threshold required before surfacing to
                                  executive level.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Architecture Component**      **Definition**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Confidence Types**            Data Confidence · Inference Confidence
                                  · Narrative Confidence · Recommendation
                                  Confidence · Readiness Confidence ·
                                  Domain Confidence · Executive
                                  Confidence.

  **Evidence Lineage**            Structure: Signal → Evidence →
                                  Inference → Confidence →
                                  Recommendation. Every material
                                  intelligence output must trace this
                                  chain completely.

  **Confidence Propagation**      Confidence flows across domains.
                                  Supplier confirmation improves Business Resilience
                                  confidence, risk confidence, resilience
                                  confidence, financial confidence. An
                                  enterprise confidence graph, not
                                  isolated scoring.

  **Multi-Source Conflict         A conflicting intelligence element is a
  Resolution**                    first-class object, not a domain-local
                                  row. It carries its own identity and a
                                  list of affected domains as metadata
                                  --- it does not belong to any single
                                  domain. It is resolved exactly once, at
                                  a single resolution surface, never
                                  re-resolved independently inside each
                                  affected domain. On resolution, every
                                  domain and Sacred 12 screen referencing
                                  that element updates simultaneously.
                                  The superseded value and its source are
                                  never deleted --- both are retained
                                  permanently in the evidence chain,
                                  visible in the audit trail, even after
                                  a winning value is chosen. One
                                  decision, one record, many consumers.

  **Evidence Accessibility**      A source label is not evidence --- a
                                  link is. Every intelligence element,
                                  contested or not, must resolve to a
                                  clickable reference: the source
                                  document, the specific page or section,
                                  the extraction method (parsed table,
                                  OCR, NLP inference), and the extraction
                                  timestamp. This applies uniformly to a
                                  single uncontested value and to every
                                  competing value in a conflict --- the
                                  human resolving a conflict must be able
                                  to open each source, not just read its
                                  name. Dense summary screens (domain
                                  rows, Q1--Q12 answers, Sacred 12
                                  metrics) show a one-line source label
                                  only; the full evidence chain lives in
                                  the Evidence Intelligence Center
                                  (Section 14.1.3) and is always one
                                  click away --- never reconstructed
                                  independently per screen.

  **Confidence Decay Engine**     Truth gets stale. Confidence weakens
                                  over time. CorpStage tracks age and
                                  applies decay. Supplier review 18
                                  months old → confidence decreases →
                                  refresh recommended.

  **Contradiction Architecture**  Actively detects: Stated vs Observed ·
                                  Strategy vs Budget · Commitment vs
                                  Action · Target vs Resource Allocation
                                  · Disclosure vs Operational Reality.
                                  Powers Screens 10--12 heavily.

  **Explainability Layer**        Executives can always ask: Why?
                                  CorpStage answers: Why this conclusion?
                                  · Why this confidence? · What evidence?
                                  · What assumptions? · What changed?

  **Executive Trust Index**       Measures how trustworthy CorpStage
                                  currently is for this enterprise. Based
                                  on: evidence coverage · confidence
                                  quality · contradiction resolution ·
                                  freshness · human validation ·
                                  readiness maturity.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

| **Step | **Enterprise Interaction Model**                            |
| 11**   |                                                             |
|        | *How humans and CorpStage work together. The burden of      |
|        | effort shifts from humans to the system.*                   |
+========+=============================================================+
+--------+-------------------------------------------------------------+

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Foundational Principle**                                            |
|                                                                       |
| Wrong model: User drives system. Upload everything. Fill forms.       |
| Maintain records. Chase stakeholders.                                 |
|                                                                       |
| CorpStage model: CorpStage Understands → CorpStage Infers → CorpStage |
| Clarifies → Humans Resolve Ambiguity → Intelligence Strengthens.      |
|                                                                       |
| Humans should feel: \"CorpStage understands my business.\" Not: \"I   |
| need to feed the system.\"                                            |
+=======================================================================+
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Interaction Stage**           **What happens and how**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Stage 1 --- Understand**      Learn enterprise context. Method:
                                  extraction, retrieval, minimal
                                  questions. No onboarding fatigue.

  **Stage 2 --- Observe**         Continuously watch enterprise signals
                                  --- internal reality, external reality,
                                  supplier ecosystem, market shifts,
                                  regulations, contradictions. CorpStage
                                  works silently.

  **Stage 3 --- Infer**           Reduce uncertainty. \"We believe
                                  supplier concentration risk is
                                  elevated.\" No user effort yet.

  **Stage 4 --- Confirm**         Preferred interaction. \"We believe 4
                                  suppliers are operationally critical.
                                  Correct?\" Options: Confirm / Adjust /
                                  Delegate.

  **Stage 5 --- Correct**         Improve understanding. \"One supplier
                                  is strategically irreplaceable.\"
                                  Refinement over manual entry.

  **Stage 6 --- Delegate**        Send to closest source of truth:
                                  Procurement → supplier dependency ·
                                  Finance → debt sensitivity · HR →
                                  workforce · Legal → entity boundary ·
                                  Executive → strategic commitment.

  **Stage 7 --- Escalate**        Handle ambiguity or contradiction.
                                  Triggered by: conflicting signals, low
                                  confidence, strategic uncertainty,
                                  executive materiality.

  **Stage 8 --- Recommend**       Guide action. Never decide. \"Supplier
                                  diversification discussion may be
                                  warranted.\"
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

| **Guided Completion Experience --- The Strongest UX Differentiator**  |
|                                                                       |
| Good: \"High Impact Opportunity --- Spend 3 minutes. Potential gains: |
| +12% Supplier Intelligence. Also improves: Operational Risk ·         |
| Regulatory Cost Exposure · Financial Exposure modelling.\"            |
|                                                                       |
| Not: \"Please complete section 8.\"                                   |
|                                                                       |
| Enterprise Effort Score: \"Estimated manual effort avoided: 46        |
| hours.\" Very strong enterprise ROI signal.                           |

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Foundational Principle**                                            |
|                                                                       |
| Not all intelligence deserves attention. CorpStage optimises for      |
| executive attention --- not information completeness.                 |
|                                                                       |
| Wrong model: Show everything. 50 KPIs. 100 alerts. Red-yellow-green   |
| overload. Result: executives stop paying attention.                   |
|                                                                       |
| CorpStage model: Show what matters most now. Suppress everything      |
| else. Create calm executive cognition.                                |
|                                                                       |
| Core rule: Every intelligence point must answer \"Why now?\" If no    |
| answer: stay silent.                                                  |

**Priority Score Formula (Locked)**

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  *Priority Score = Materiality × Financial Impact × Confidence Gap ×
  Urgency × Executive Relevance × Cross-Domain Impact × Contradiction
  Severity × Ease of Resolution*
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Prioritization Category**     **Definition and examples**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Category 1 --- Immediate      \"Leadership should see now.\"
  Executive Attention**           Criteria: high materiality, financial
                                  exposure, contradictions, strategic
                                  importance. Surfaces: Sacred 12,
                                  Executive Home. Examples: supplier
                                  dependency risk, margin pressure,
                                  leadership inconsistency.

  **Category 2 --- Guided         \"High-value improvement opportunity.\"
  Intelligence Completion**       Example: \"Spend 4 mins → Supplier
                                  Intelligence +12%, Regulatory Cost
                                  Exposure +9%, Operational Risk
                                  confidence +7%.\" High leverage for
                                  minimal effort.

  **Category 3 --- Functional     \"Relevant but not executive.\" Route
  Attention**                     to Operations, not CEO. Example:
                                  facility-level waste inconsistency.
                                  Critical routing --- executive
                                  attention is finite.

  **Category 4 --- Background     \"Observe silently.\" No interruption.
  Monitoring**                    Examples: benchmark updates, minor
                                  regulation shifts, low materiality
                                  signals. CorpStage watches quietly.
                                  Very premium behaviour.

  **Category 5 --- Suppressed     \"Do not surface.\" Criteria:
  Intelligence**                  immaterial, redundant, stale, low
                                  confidence, low impact. Huge
                                  differentiator. Most systems fail here.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Prioritization Principle**    **How it works**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Signal Escalation Logic**     Small supplier issue → supplier
                                  concentration worsens → criticality
                                  threshold crossed → executive
                                  attention. Triggers: confidence drop,
                                  contradiction emergence, financial
                                  impact increase, regulation tightening.

  **Contradiction                 Contradictions should rank highly ---
  Prioritization**                they reveal organisational truth.
                                  Commitment vs Funding · Strategy vs
                                  Operations · Disclosure vs Evidence ·
                                  Stated Priority vs Budget.

  **Executive Attention Budget**  Maximum surfaced priorities: up to 7
                                  priorities --- no minimum enforced,
                                  never more than 7. Never 47
                                  notifications. This is premium.
                                  Cognitive ceiling is non-negotiable.

  **Personalization Layer**       CEO: enterprise resilience, strategic
                                  contradictions. CFO: financial
                                  materiality. COO: operational
                                  fragility. Procurement: supplier
                                  dependencies. Same intelligence.
                                  Different prioritization.

  **Silent Intelligence           Most intelligence should remain
  Principle**                     invisible unless needed. Executives
                                  feel: \"CorpStage seems thoughtful.\"
                                  Not: \"CorpStage overwhelms me.\"
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| **Executive Priority Narrative --- The Golden Standard**              |
|                                                                       |
| Instead of: 42 issues.                                                |
|                                                                       |
| CorpStage surfaces:                                                   |
|                                                                       |
| \"What matters now:                                                   |
|                                                                       |
| • Supplier dependency may be creating concentrated operational risk.  |
|                                                                       |
| • Leadership commitments appear stronger than funding alignment.      |
|                                                                       |
| • Transition Cost Exposure is emerging as a medium-term financial         |
| pressure.\"                                                           |
|                                                                       |
| Golden Rule: CorpStage should maximize signal, minimize noise.        |
| Executive attention is the scarcest enterprise resource.              |

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **14.1 --- Phase 1 Enterprise Foundation Screens SIM**
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The three Foundation screens exist before the Sacred 12. They build the
enterprise understanding that makes every Sacred 12 screen meaningful.
Without them, the cognition screens become shallow.

+----------+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| **       | **Enterprise Understanding Center SIM**                   |
| 14.1.1** |                                                           |
|          |                                                           |
| Full     |                                                           |
+==========+===========================================================+
+----------+-----------------------------------------------------------+

**1. Executive Purpose**

Build a progressively intelligent understanding of the organization with
minimal human effort. This screen exists not for onboarding, not for
setup, not for master data entry --- but to help CorpStage understand
enough about the business to begin meaningful intelligence synthesis.

Outcome: CorpStage understands enough about the business to begin
meaningful intelligence synthesis.

**2. Organizational Truth**

Core truth: \"How does this enterprise actually function?\" --- not what
the company says it is, but what operational, financial, organizational
and ecosystem reality suggests it truly is.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Sub-Truth**                   **What CorpStage must reveal**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Enterprise Identity**         Who are we? Company profile, industry,
                                  sector, ownership model,
                                  listed/private, regions, legal
                                  footprint.

  **Enterprise Structure**        How are we organized? Legal entities,
                                  subsidiaries, business units, operating
                                  entities, reporting hierarchy, shared
                                  services.

  **Operating Reality**           How do we actually operate? Facilities,
                                  manufacturing/service footprint,
                                  logistics, supply chain model,
                                  operational dependencies.

  **Value Creation**              How do we make money?
                                  Products/services, revenue drivers,
                                  business segments, cost structure,
                                  value chain, margin drivers.

  **Ecosystem Dependency**        Who do we depend on? Strategic
                                  suppliers, supplier concentration,
                                  vendor criticality, partner
                                  dependencies, customer concentration.

  **Strategic Context**           What matters to leadership? Strategic
                                  priorities, transformation initiatives,
                                  operational ambitions, declared
                                  commitments.

  **Operational Exposure**        Where are we vulnerable? Regulatory
                                  exposure, geographic risk, climate
                                  exposure, geopolitical exposure,
                                  competitive pressure.

  **Confidence Gaps**             What do we still not understand? What
                                  is known, what is inferred, what is
                                  weakly understood, what is missing.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Domain**                      **Must understand**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **A. Enterprise Identity**      Company profile, industry, sector,
                                  ownership model, listed/private,
                                  regions, legal footprint.

  **B. Organisational Structure** Legal entities, subsidiaries, business

                                  hierarchy, shared services.

                                  business segments, cost structure,
                                  value chain, margin drivers.

  **D. Operating Model**          Facilities, manufacturing/service
                                  footprint, logistics, supply chain
                                  model, operational dependencies,
                                  geographic concentration.

  **E. Supplier & Ecosystem**     Strategic suppliers, supplier
                                  concentration, vendor criticality,
                                  partner dependencies, customer
                                  concentration.

  **F. Financial Context**        Revenue profile, cost structure, capex
                                  intensity, debt sensitivity, margin
                                  pressure, financial priorities.

  **G. Workforce & Capability**   Workforce structure, critical talent
                                  areas, contractor dependence,

  **H. Governance & Leadership**  Leadership structure, accountability,

**9. Business Question Architecture**

CorpStage never asks framework questions. CorpStage never asks
data-entry questions. CorpStage asks business understanding questions.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Principle**                   **Rule**
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------
  **Question Hierarchy (Locked)** Level 1 --- Confirm (Fastest,
                                  Preferred) → Level 2 --- Correct
                                  (Refine) → Level 3 --- Clarify (Resolve
                                  ambiguity) → Level 4 --- Contextualize
                                  (Add nuance) → Level 5 --- Ask (Last
                                  resort only). Golden Rule: never
                                  reverse this order.

  **Wrong Questions**             ❌ \"Enter Scope 3 emissions\" · ❌
                                  \"Provide ESG metrics\" · ❌ \"Upload
                                  workforce diversity data\" · ❌
                                  \"Complete Section 8\"

  **CorpStage Questions**         ✅ \"Which suppliers would materially
                                  disrupt operations if unavailable?\" ·
                                  ✅ \"Which facilities are most critical
                                  to business continuity?\" · ✅ \"What
                                  costs create the most pressure on
                                  profitability?\"

  **Guided Completion Design**    Package questions as High Leverage
                                  Opportunities. Show: time required,
                                  improvement expected, domains improved.
                                  Never: \"Complete supplier section.\"

  **Question Suppression Rules**  Do NOT ask when: already extractable ·
                                  inferable confidently · low materiality
                                  · duplicate knowledge · weak business
                                  value.

  **Question Tone**               Calm · Intelligent · Respectful ·
                                  Executive-grade · Non-accusatory ·
                                  Low-friction. Never: interrogative ·
                                  compliance-heavy · bureaucratic ·
                                  audit-like.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
